title: Marketplace listing lightning checklist + standup notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick, tactical checklist + standup note doc for publishing partner listings across AWS Marketplace, Azure Marketplace, and GCP Marketplace when we need to move fast. This is intentionally light — use as sprint-day reference and handoff to Ops/Legal if blockers remain.

Outcomes we want by EOD launch window:
- Basic listing copy live (tile + short description + 1 feature bullet list)
- Pricing SKU mapped and verified with finance (billing SKU + metering nomenclature)
- Technical acceptance (image, download, connector URL, or SaaS callback validated)
- Compliance gating (privacy snippet + security contact + required certificates referenced)
- Marketing assets queued (tile artwork, 1-page datasheet, 2 social copy variants)

Owner & role matrix (who does what in a lightning launch):
- Listing owner: Aisha Patel — final copy signoff, marketplace submission, vendor profile fields.
- Technical validator: Marcus Chen — verifies connector endpoints, health check URL, auth flow for each marketplace.
- Pricing & billing: Lena Ortiz — confirm SKU mapping, price tiers, trial handling.
- Legal/compliance checkpoint: Ravi Sundaram — privacy language + required attestations.
- Creative & marketing: Tasha Nguyen — artwork, social copy, and landing page gating.

Minimal acceptance checklist (must be green for any marketplace):
1) Tile & short description: 1 line title (<=60 chars), short description (<=140 chars). Avoid product jargon, put value-first.
2) Long description: 3–4 short paragraphs + 3 bullets describing capabilities and typical customer scenarios. Include one compliance sentence (e.g., "Data is not retained beyond inference unless customer opts in").
3) Feature bullets: 3–6 short bullets; include throughput/latency highlight if relevant (e.g., "predictable p99 latency for dedicated pools").
4) Pricing mapping: SKU id, billing cadence, free trial (yes/no), metering unit (tokens / requests / seats), link to finance ticket.
5) Technical artifact: deployment package or SaaS callback URL + healthcheck endpoint + expected response schema.
6) Contact fields: support email, security contact, SA/solutions contact.
7) Legal check: T&Cs pointer + data handling blurb included.
8) Assets: 1 hero tile (1200x600), 3 supporting screenshots, 1-page PDF datasheet.
9) Internal tags & metadata: product category, audience (SMB/Enterprise), recommended plan, managed vs. self-hosted flag.
10) Smoke test: Basic provisioning flow completes end-to-end (create account -> provision -> get token -> inference call) within 10 minutes.

Marketplace-specific quick notes:
- AWS: Requires AMS listing template. Ensure listing SKU & AMI (if used) fields are consistent with finance mapping. Upload tile image in PNG and also supply 16:9 JPG. Add 1-line partner blurb for "About the seller".
- Azure: Confirm Azure AD OAuth redirect URIs for SaaS listings and tenant onboarding script if applicable. Check pricing units translated to Azure metering format.
- GCP: Verify OAuth client id allowed redirect URIs and any service account artifacts. GCP acceptance sometimes requires extra security questionnaire; flag early.

Copy snippets (lightweight options to iterate quickly):
- Tile title (option A): "Redwood Inference — Predictable LLM inference"
- Tile title (option B): "Redwood Inference: Low-latency LLM serving"
- Short description: "High-throughput inference for LLMs with predictable latency and cost controls — hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
- 3-line feature bullets (short form):
  • "Hosted API for fast time-to-value, plus private deployments for regulated workloads."
  • "Intelligent batching and KV caching to cut token cost without sacrificing latency."
  • "Dedicated GPU pools with SLA-backed performance for production workloads."
- CTA: "Try a free trial or contact sales for a dedicated capacity evaluation."

Common acceptance blockers we've seen (triage heuristics):
- Missing billing SKU or mismatched price tiers between listing and finance spreadsheet -> escalate to Lena.
- Healthcheck endpoint returns 500 on cold start -> Marcus to coordinate infra fix and add retry guidance in docs.
- Creative assets wrong dimensions or license issues -> Tasha to supply new files and tag for compliance.
- Legal needs additional data processing addendum -> Ravi to route to LegalOps and mark listing hold.

Standup notes (live sprint day log):
- 08:30: Kickoff — agreed to target GCP + AWS simultaneous submit; Azure to follow in next sprint.
- 09:10: Copy draft posted to PR, awaiting owner signoff (Aisha).
- 10:00: Marcus validated healthcheck for SaaS flow on staging (token exchange OK).
- 11:45: Finance checkpoint found mismatch in metering unit for trial SKU — Lena updating GM-1402.
- 13:20: Legal flagged security questionnaire for GCP — Ravi requested pre-fill and expects turnaround by EOD.
- 15:05: Creative sent final hero tile plus 3 screenshots; sizes OK for AWS, needs 1 cropped version for Azure thumbnail.
- 16:30: Smoke test passed on AWS staging; GCP smoke test failing intermittently (502) — Marcus investigating autoscaler config.

Immediate action items (owner in parentheses):
- Update listing long copy with compliance sentence and 1 enterprise use-case (Aisha).
- Finish price table reconciliation and attach finance ticket (Lena).
- Upload Azure-specific thumbnail variant (Tasha).
- Complete GCP security questionnaire draft and tag LegalOps (Ravi).
- Add a small troubleshooting note in the tech docs for 502 on initial provision (Marcus).

Templates & quick links to paste during submission:
- One-line title formula: [Product] — [Primary benefit] (<=60 chars)
- Short desc formula: [What it does] + [Primary customer outcome] + [Deployment options]
- Long desc skeleton: 1) Problem statement; 2) How Redwood solves it; 3) Key capabilities (bulleted); 4) Who should use it; 5) Links to docs & support.

Notes for follow-up sprint (non-blocking):
- Prepare a canned A/B copy test for tile titles (performance on conversion) and run for 2 weeks post-launch.
- Add a quick internal KB article for "Marketplace smoke tests" that SREs can run (checklist + scripts).
- Align marketing on a one-week social cadence post-publish with 2 creative variants.

Slack channels & PR pointers to mention in submission comments:
- #gm-marketplace (primary ops thread)
- #prod-infra (if provisioning issues arise)
- PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/marketplace-assets/pull/56 (copy + assets), github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/112 (docs link)

Questions unresolved (parking lot):
- Do we want to surface "quantization" as a selling bullet in the tile copy? Risk: too much jargon for marketplace buyers. (Decision: keep it in long description only unless audience is clearly developer-heavy.)
- SLA language: use percent uptime vs. "SLA-backed" phrase. Need legal guidance.

Quick checklist for final publish (tick when done):
[ ] Title and short description signed off
[ ] Long description uploaded
[ ] Pricing SKU confirmed and finance ticket linked
[ ] Tech artifacts validated and smoke test green
[ ] Creative assets uploaded (tile + screenshots + datasheet)
[ ] Legal/compliance signed off (or escalated with note)
[ ] Submission created and confirmation screenshot attached to PR

If anything blocks for >2 hours, escalate in #gm-marketplace and ping on-call SRE if infra-related.

End of doc — keep this as the quick sprint reference. Copy into Confluence when stabilized (confluence: marketplace-lightning-playbook).
